research_scope: Source-free mathematical prerequisite identity audit against original formulation text; parent scope and stronger structural conditions remain distinct.

aliases.reason: The locally-finite-collection statement and local Krull-dimension statement both quantify over an open neighborhood U of a point x: x∈U∈τ. The selection for every point and the finite-family-intersection condition are parent-level; this is not merged with a more general, possibly nonopen neighborhood convention.

The local-complete-intersection algebra definition uses standard principal opens D(g_i) in Spec(S), and the scheme topology uses D(f) in Spec(R). Both are the distinguished Zariski opens D(h)={p:h∉p} of an affine prime spectrum. Covering hypotheses and localizations are separately retained.

Mutual independence and pairwise independence both begin with the same indexed measurable event family (A_i) on one probability space, with A_i in the sigma algebra. They differ in the finite-intersection versus pairwise product equations, which remain attached to the parent independence notions, not the event-family prerequisite.

The projective-summand source uses R^(I) as a free module of finitely supported functions on I, and the free-resolution source uses arbitrary-rank free modules F_i. Both require the same free R-module with a basis, equivalently a direct sum of copies of R; the free resolution and summand properties remain separate.

The general random-variable source describes X:(Ω,F)→(S,Σ_S) as measurable iff inverse images of Σ_S sets belong to F; the pushforward-measure source uses the same condition for f:(X,Σ)→(Y,T). They share measurable-map semantics; the probability-measure requirement, measure pushforward, and naming as a random variable are separate parent context.
